title: Complementary quantum and classical records of qubit decoherence
summary: Decoherence is usually viewed as the loss of local coherence, but it also writes information into the environment. Here we show that the environment stores this information in two distinct forms. One is a recoverable quantum record: after a transverse qubit measurement, the bath is projected onto a Schrödinger-cat-like state in a mode-matched physical collective coordinate. The other is a redundant classical which-path record distributed across physical frequency-band fragments. Using tensor-network simulations of a spin--boson reservoir, we reconstruct the conditional bath Wigner function…
